name: onboard-new-source
query: We need to start pulling data from a vendor's Postgres database into our lakehouse. What's the right way to land it?
why: Source onboarding, the most common front-line moment. The answer turns on the source's change-capture capability, which is a profiling question before it is a tooling one.

name: cdc-mechanism-choice
query: Should we use log-based replication or just poll on a last_modified column?
why: Change-capture mechanism selection. The trap is that cursor polling cannot see deletes or intermediate states, which is a downstream correctness problem rather than a latency preference.

name: silent-row-loss
query: Some rows never show up in our silver tables but every pipeline run is green. Where do I even start?
why: The signature symptom in the failure index. Must fire so the symptom gets classified as scope, extract, or downstream predicate before anything is widened.

name: dbt-project-review
query: Can you review how our dbt project is laid out? We have about 200 models and it's getting hard to navigate.
why: dbt project design, and the case the manifest auditor serves.

name: incremental-strategy
query: My incremental model on Databricks keeps leaving stale rows behind even though it runs in full mode.
why: The dynamic-partition-overwrite footgun stated as a symptom. High-value trigger because every run reports success.

name: profile-unfamiliar-source
query: I've been given access to a source system nobody here has used before. What do I check before we commit to it?
why: Profiling as an admission gate. The deliverable is a go/no-go plus either a change request to the source owner or a screen specification.

name: validation-suite-design
query: What data quality checks should we actually be running on this pipeline, and where do they go?
why: Validation design, including the response policy for a failed check and the trap of a check that cannot fail.

name: bill-grew
query: Our platform bill nearly doubled last month and the data volume didn't change. Help me work out why.
why: Cost diagnosis. Turns on establishing the billing unit before proposing a lever.

name: forecast-before-commitment
query: I have to give the client a spend estimate for this platform before we sign anything. How do I approach it?
why: Cost at architecture altitude. The skill teaches drivers and guardrails rather than worked list prices, and should say so.

name: bundle-promotion
query: How should I promote these jobs from dev to prod with asset bundles?
why: Deployment, including the development-versus-production mode mechanism and the channel-sequencing law.

name: terraform-vs-workload
query: Should our catalogs and schemas be created in Terraform or in the deployment config with the jobs?
why: The layer seam stated as the user's own question. One of the two standard violations.

name: governance-setup
query: We need to set up column masking and row filters for PII across a few dozen tables. What's the right structure?
why: Governance mechanics, and the per-object grant to tag-driven policy migration.

name: dedup-matching
query: We have customer records from four systems with no shared ID and we need one record per customer.
why: Entity resolution and survivorship. The separable-problems point is the value: matching is technical, survivorship is a business rule set that has to be elicited.

name: inherited-platform-audit
query: I just took over someone else's Databricks setup. How do I work out what's actually here and whether it's any good?
why: Brownfield judgment at architecture altitude, which is a different task from building something new.

name: slow-merge
query: This MERGE takes forty minutes on a table that isn't that big. What's wrong with it?
why: Line-of-code altitude on optimization. Should reach triage order and layout, not generic SQL advice.

name: grain-question-routes-away
query: Should one row of my sales fact table be an order, an order line, or a shipment?
why: Grain belongs to dimensional-data-modeling, which should fire instead. This skill must not poach it, or the two compete for one trigger and both lose.

name: scd-question-routes-away
query: Customers move between segments. Do I overwrite the segment or keep the old value?
why: SCD semantics belong to dimensional-data-modeling, which should fire instead. This skill owns how history gets loaded, not what history should mean.

name: rag-pipeline
query: I need to chunk and embed these documents and put them in a vector store for retrieval.
why: AI engineering. Adjacent vocabulary (pipeline, ingestion, embeddings) makes this the most likely false positive.

name: dockerfile-build
query: My Docker image is 3GB and takes forever to build. How do I slim it down?
why: Container work belongs to the docker skill, even though image builds appear in the deployment layer stack.

name: generic-sql-rewrite
query: Rewrite this query to use a CTE instead of a subquery so it reads better.
why: Readability refactor with no platform, pipeline or cost dimension. Guards against firing on anything SQL-shaped.
